expectations.text: Q&A covers detection markers (class inheritance + __table__), file patterns, entity extraction (class_pattern, table_pattern, column_pattern), and at least one relationship pattern
expectations.evidence: qa-transcript.md Turn 1 section 1 covers file patterns ('`detection.file_patterns` (glob — e.g. `**/*.py`...'); section 2 covers detection markers ('base class (BaseModel, Entity, etc.)', '__table__', '__columns__'); section 3 covers entity extraction naming class_pattern, table_pattern, and column_pattern explicitly; section 4 covers relationships ('one_to_many, many_to_one, many_to_many, foreign_key' with concrete ForeignKey example). Turn 2 answers all with concrete values and the final YAML has a ForeignKey\\( relationship pattern.

expectations.text: Q&A covers naming conventions (table_from_class and column_from_field)
expectations.evidence: qa-transcript.md Turn 1 section 5 explicitly asks for both keys: 'table_from_class: lower_case | snake_case | snake_case_plural' and 'column_from_field: typically snake_case'. Turn 2 answers both: 'tables are plural snake_case (User → users). Columns are already snake_case in source so column_from_field: snake_case'.

expectations.text: Generated YAML has every required top-level field: name, language, description, detection, entity_extraction, relationship_patterns, naming_conventions
expectations.evidence: yaml.load on custom-basemodel.yaml yields top-level keys ['name','language','description','detection','entity_extraction','relationship_detection','naming_conventions']. The YAML follows the canonical shipped schema (matches sqlalchemy.yaml/django.yaml exactly) where relationship patterns are nested under relationship_detection.patterns; the loader surfaces this as profile.relationship_patterns (confirmed in profile-load-test.txt line 12: 'relationship_patterns: OK ([{"pattern":"ForeignKey\\(","type":"foreign_key"}])'). All seven required semantic fields are present and populated.

expectations.text: entity_extraction.class_pattern has a single capture group that matches at least one class name in example.py (verified by running the pattern against the fixture)
expectations.evidence: Ran `new RegExp('class\\s+(\\w+)\\s*\\(\\s*BaseModel\\s*\\)', 'gm')` against example.py: 3 matches, each with exactly one capture group. Captured names: 'User' (index 241), 'Post' (index 338), 'Comment' (index 501). m.length-1 === 1 for all matches, confirming single capture group. Helper classes BaseModel and ForeignKey are correctly excluded (neither inherits from BaseModel).

expectations.text: profile loader (profiles.js loadProfile) accepts the YAML without raising ProfileValueError
expectations.evidence: Executed `loadProfile('/Users/narayan/src/doc-wiki/wiki-workspace/iteration-3/orm-agent-custom-profile/with_skill/outputs/custom-basemodel.yaml')` — returned a populated OrmProfile with keys [name, language, description, file_patterns, markers, class_pattern, table_pattern, column_pattern, relationship_patterns, naming_conventions]. No exception thrown. Matches the claim in profile-load-test.txt.

expectations.text: When the profile is applied to example.py, extractEntities yields at least one ExtractedEntity per BaseModel class in the fixture — not all classes collapsing to a single table
expectations.evidence: Ran `extractEntities({[examplePath]: content}, profile)` and got 3 entities: User/table_name=users, Post/table_name=posts, Comment/table_name=comments. new Set([users,posts,comments]).size === 3 — all DIFFERENT, each matching the corresponding __table__ literal in the fixture. The profile's deliberate __tablename__ vs __table__ mismatch forces the classToTable fallback (snake_case_plural), producing per-class tables without collapse.

claims.claim: table_pattern deliberately mismatches __table__ to force the classToTable naming-convention fallback at extractor.ts:137-140, avoiding the per-class collapse
claims.evidence: Confirmed by running extractEntities — the profile's table_pattern `__tablename__\s*=\s*['"]([\w.]+)['"]` never matches in the fixture (which uses `__table__`, not `__tablename__`), so every class falls through to classToTable with snake_case_plural. Result: User→users, Post→posts, Comment→comments — exactly the __table__ literals. Verified in profile.ts loader chain and confirmed extractEntities produced 3 unique table_name values.

claims.claim: class_pattern excludes the BaseModel and ForeignKey helper classes (entity count = 3, not 5)
claims.evidence: class_pattern requires `(BaseModel)` as parent; ForeignKey has no parent list and BaseModel inherits from object. Regex produces exactly 3 matches: User, Post, Comment. extractEntities returns exactly 3 entities.

claims.claim: Extracted table names equal the __table__ literals exactly, despite table_pattern being intentionally non-matching
claims.evidence: users==users, posts==posts, comments==comments — all three match. The naming-convention fallback happens to produce identical strings because the team's table naming discipline (plural snake_case) agrees with snake_case_plural inference. Not guaranteed for all ORMs, but correct for this fixture.

claims.claim: column_pattern captures per-class columns from __columns__ list literals
claims.evidence: column_pattern `['"](\w+)['"]` is overly broad — it captures EVERY quoted identifier in the file, including class names inside ForeignKey(...) calls and strings in every class's __columns__. extractEntities attaches ~20 columns to every entity (identical across all three classes), rather than the 3-5 columns per class the fixture actually declares. The agent claimed 'captures every quoted string in __columns__ list literals' (Q&A Turn 2) but the pattern is not scoped to __columns__ — any quoted word anywhere is captured. The per-class table assertion still passes because table_name is computed independently of columns, but column extraction is incorrect.

needs_review: column_pattern is not scoped to __columns__ list literals; it matches every quoted identifier in the source file, producing identical ~20-entry column lists across all three entities. This was not caught by any assertion.
workarounds: Deliberately non-matching table_pattern (`__tablename__` vs fixture's `__table__`) forces every entity through the naming-convention fallback. This is an acknowledged trade-off documented in qa-transcript.md Turn 2 and the YAML description.

suggestions.assertion: Generated YAML has every required top-level field: name, language, description, detection, entity_extraction, relationship_patterns, naming_conventions
suggestions.reason: The canonical shipped schema nests relationship patterns under `relationship_detection.patterns` at the YAML layer; the loader exposes it as `relationship_patterns` only on the OrmProfile object. The assertion wording conflates the two layers and could either (a) be interpreted strictly (fail, since YAML has `relationship_detection`, not `relationship_patterns`) or (b) loosely (pass, since the semantic field is present). Consider restating as 'YAML contains relationship_detection.patterns (or equivalent)' or 'loader surfaces profile.relationship_patterns with >=1 entry' to make the check unambiguous.

No assertion verifies that the generated column_pattern actually captures only __columns__ entries rather than any quoted identifier. When I ran extractEntities the returned entities each had ~20 columns (including class names like 'User', 'Post' and parameter strings like 'user_id' from ForeignKey calls) because the profile's column_pattern `['"](\w+)['"]` is unscoped. The per-class table_name check passes but column extraction is effectively broken. An assertion like 'extractEntities(User).columns contains only [id, email, created_at] and excludes strings from other classes' would catch this.

No assertion verifies that table_pattern actually works for the intended fixture. The agent chose to make table_pattern deliberately non-matching as a workaround for the single-file collapse issue. This is clever, but an eval author might want to catch that the profile relies on a fallback rather than on the documented table_pattern — e.g. 'running table_pattern against example.py yields at least 3 matches' would surface the design choice.

eval_feedback.overall: All 6 assertions pass with solid evidence, but the evals miss a real defect (broken column extraction) and one assertion has ambiguous wording around YAML vs OrmProfile field names. Tightening the column-extraction assertion would make future iterations more discriminating.
